title: I Hope GTA 6 Borrows a Lot From GTA 4, Says IGN
description: Playing GTA 4 for the first time since 2008 has sparked discussions on what elements Rockstar should borrow for GTA 6.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Revisiting a Classic: Why GTA 4 Still Matters

Ever since its release in 2008, Grand Theft Auto 4 has held a distinct and revered place in the hearts of open-world gaming fans. Recently, a gaming media outlet revisited the title for the first time since its launch year, sparking a compelling conversation about what Rockstar Games should consider borrowing from it for the highly anticipated GTA 6.

While Grand Theft Auto 5 undoubtedly redefined modern gaming commerce and set massive standards for open-world scale, many long-time fans often look back at GTA 4 for its gritty realism, physics engine, and unmatched attention to urban detail. As anticipation builds for the next installment set in Vice City, the gaming community continues to ponder how Rockstar will balance technological innovation with the deep immersion found in past titles.

## Expectations and Potential Inspirations for GTA 6

Looking back at what made GTA 4 stand out, features like its advanced physics and reactive NPC behaviors created a living, breathing world that felt remarkably grounded. Although these reflections are based on revisiting an older title rather than official announcements, they highlight a persistent desire from players for tangible weight, immersive storytelling, and intricate world-building in modern sandbox games.

As we await further official updates regarding GTA 6, it remains to be seen precisely which legacy mechanics Rockstar chooses to incorporate into the upcoming title.

## Editor's Take

At GTA6 Hub, we believe looking back at GTA 4 reminds us that true immersion goes beyond map size or graphical fidelity. If GTA 6 can successfully blend modern next-gen capabilities with the raw, gritty detail and reactive world design of its 2008 predecessor, we are truly in for a masterpiece.
